content: 1. Hydromorphone, which constitutes less than 3% of circulating hydrocodone, is primarily formed through CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation of hydrocodone. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 3. Co-administration of hydrocodone with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma concentrations of hydrocodone, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 4. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. 5. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. 6. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. 7. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of hydromorphone by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 10. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates should be avoided. 11. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Lopinavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Ritonavir increases the effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting hepatic CYP2B6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Co-administration of ifosfamide with CYP2B6 inducers may increase the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active metabolite. Monitoring for increased effects or toxicities is necessary. 16. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. 17. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. 18. Iloperidone increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Iloperidone increases the levels of lopinavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 21. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Indacaterol, when inhaled, may prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 24. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. 25. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels of inhaled indacaterol by modulating both P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. 28. Indinavir and ritonavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 29. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. 30. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. 31. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. 32. Ritonavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart by inducing insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Lopinavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart by inducing insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and induce hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 35. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 49. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. 51. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 52. Do not exceed istradefylline 20 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 53. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 54. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 55. Limit itraconazole dose to 200 mg/day in patients receiving ritonavir. 56. Ivacaftor increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema when amlodipine is co-administered with CYP3A inhibitors to determine the need for dose adjustment. 91.
